title: ClaimReuseAuthorization
description: The verifier-policy decision about whether each claim-scoped semantic attestation carried by one revision-plan trace may be reused for the current draft. It is a separate artifact from the revision-plan trace and from the v0.1 AuditTrace. Every decision is claim-scoped: this artifact never issues a whole-document PASS, never releases a document, and never asserts that a claim is true. A stored decision is not authoritative on its own; a reader MUST replay it against the revision-plan trace, which recomputes every hash and every decision.

authorizationId.description: Envelope metadata outside evaluationHash. Not authenticated provenance.

createdAt.description: Envelope metadata outside evaluationHash. An edit to it is not detectable from this artifact alone, and it may not be relied on as evidence of when a decision was made.

extractorVersion.description: The extractor version recorded in the revision-plan trace. A reuse authorization inherits that extractor's protected-fingerprint judgement and is only as strong as it.

asOf.description: The caller-supplied deterministic evaluation instant every freshness gate is measured against. It is bound by evaluationHash. It is deterministic input, not authenticated time.

policyHash.description: hashObject over the stored canonical policy. A reader MUST recompute it from the stored policy rather than trust it.

decisions.description: One decision per mapped bound attestation, canonically sorted ascending and unique by boundAttestationHash. The runtime reader additionally rejects an unordered or duplicated array.

evaluationHash.description: hashObject over schemaVersion, kind, engineVersion, extractorVersion, asOf, policyHash, policy, trace, documentRelease, decisions, and reasons. authorizationId and createdAt are excluded so the same trace, policy, and asOf reproduce the same identity.

trustedChecker.description: One allowlisted checker identity. Trust is the exact triple; a new version or a different kind is a different attestor.

claimPin.description: What one claim's attestation must carry, and what the caller declares about it. claimBindingHash, snapshotId, and evidenceHash are cryptographic gates: the attestation must carry exactly these values. A snapshot ID alone is not enough, because one snapshot serves many claims with different cited subsets. jurisdiction, domain, and sourceCurrencyConfirmedAsOf are caller declarations recorded and age-gated here; this runtime cannot read any of the three out of a SemanticAttestation and does not independently verify them. Exactly one pin per claimId is permitted.

policy.description: The closed policy input, stored in canonical order: trustedCheckers sorted by name, version, and kind; claimPins sorted by claimId. The runtime reader additionally rejects a stored policy that is not in canonical order, that duplicates a checker triple or a claimId, or that gives one checker name and version two different kinds.

minScore.description: The explicit score threshold an attestation must meet. There is no default.

maxAttestationAgeDays.description: The explicit maximum age of an attestation, measured from checkedAt to asOf. There is no clock-skew window: asOf is deterministic input, so an attestation dated after it is always refused.

maxSourceCurrencyAgeDays.description: The explicit maximum age of the caller's source-currency confirmation, measured to asOf.

traceBinding.description: The revision-plan trace this decision was evaluated against. A replay MUST be given that exact artifact; a trace whose artifactHash differs is refused rather than re-evaluated.

mappingStatus.description: COMPLETE is a precondition for any authorization, never a reason for one. Any other status refuses every decision in this artifact.

documentRelease.description: The document-level condition that survives every claim-scoped decision. Automatic candidate extraction never asserts complete coverage, so this artifact has exactly one document status and can never release a document.

blocker.description: One typed reason authorization was refused. Every blocker is fatal to REUSE_AUTHORIZED.

currentCandidate.description: The single current-draft candidate a reuse authorization applies to, located by canonical hash in the recomputed current inventory. A candidate that cannot be located uniquely refuses the decision instead of guessing a position.

decision.description: One claim-scoped decision. planIndex and planAction are present only when the mapping found exactly one plan item; the runtime reader additionally rejects them when the mapping result is NOT_IN_PLAN or AMBIGUOUS, and rejects a stored outcome that contradicts its own blockers.

mappingResult.description: Copied from the recomputed prior-attestation mapping. MATCHED_REUSE_ITEM is an association, and by itself is still not reuse authorization.

outcome.description: REUSE_AUTHORIZED authorizes reuse of this one attestation for the one named current candidate under this policy at this asOf. REVERIFY_REQUIRED means the plan says the claim changed. POLICY_BLOCKED means the named policy refused. HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED means this runtime cannot deterministically classify the claim.

blockers.description: Sorted, unique, and empty exactly when the outcome is REUSE_AUTHORIZED.
